title: Memory and Context Management
description: Manage agent memory, conversation history, and context windows so agents remain accurate over long interactions.

blocks.text: Agents need memory to remember user preferences, prior tool results, and long-term facts. Context management ensures that memory stays within the model's limits without losing important information.

blocks.title: Memory layers
items: **Short-term memory** — recent turns in the current conversation.
**Working memory** — scratchpad or plan state maintained during task execution.
**Long-term memory** — facts persisted across sessions, such as user preferences.
**Retrieval memory** — facts fetched from a knowledge base rather than stored in the prompt.

blocks.title: Strategies
items: **Summarization** — compress older turns into a brief summary.
**Sliding window** — keep only the most recent turns.
**RAG-style memory** — retrieve relevant facts from long-term memory instead of stuffing them into the prompt.

blocks.title: Avoid silent context loss
blocks.text: When you summarize or truncate history, the agent may contradict earlier statements. Log summaries and test multi-turn scenarios explicitly.

blocks.title: Implement Memory Management
blocks.description: Add memory and context management to an agent prototype.
steps: Summarize older turns when the token budget is reached.
Retrieve relevant past facts for new questions.
Measure answer consistency across long conversations.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should maintain coherent behavior over many turns without exceeding the model's context window.
